doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Joining Basie and life on the road
title: Recalling the audition and flying to New York
summary: Opening the second session, Foster restates the audition, Basie's 'we'll be in touch kid', and the telegram in July.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: The 25th of September 1998. I’m William Brower, talking with Frank Foster. Recording is Matt Watson. This is for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Program. Can you describe your coming to meet Basie, what the actual moment -- do you recollect that moment when you’re summoned and you come and you meet him? What happened? Describe that moment.
When I first joined him? You don’t mean the time I auditioned in Detroit.
I want to hear the audition, and I want to hear the first gig.

I think I’ve already said that I walked into the auditorium -- not auditorium, but dancehall. The band was playing. I walked up to -- Ernie Wilkins and Jimmy recognized me immediately. They -- I suppose introduced me to Basie. I don’t remember the moment I was introduced to Basie. All I can remember about that is I played two tunes. They played two tunes, and I was featured as soloist. I remember

Mr. Basie saying to me, “We’ll be in touch kid.” That’s the extent of my memory of that evening. Three months later, when the telegram came with the ticket to New York from Detroit, I flew to New York. I had that memorable evening during which I sat in with Charlie Parker at Birdland. The next morning I got up. The bus was supposed to leave at 6 a.m. from a place known as the Woodside Hotel, for which the song, Jumping at the Woodside is named.
